fields.name: echo_payload
fields.label: Echo payload (opaque)
fields.desc: duss_event_ping is a 3-instruction trampoline: it reads the incoming event struct's length field (struct offset 0x10) and data pointer (struct offset 0x14) and tail-calls duss_event_resp_data_v2(ctx, len, data) with them unchanged. It never inspects or validates the payload at all -- whatever bytes the sender puts here are echoed back verbatim as the response. Length and content are entirely sender-defined; in practice this is used to carry a counter/timestamp for round-trip-time or liveness checks, exactly like ICMP ping, but the wire format itself has no fixed fields.

name: Push Param Set
note: Checked, in order: (1) libduml_frwk.so's one built-in 6-entry dynamic-command table (duss_event_create_dynamic_cmd_tbl, vaddr 0x1098fc on E1E) -- fully dumped and decoded; its 6 entries are cmd_set/cmd_id {0x00/0x00, 0x00/0x2f, 0x00/0x89, 0x00/0xaa, 0x00/0xfa, 0x51/0x05}. None is 0x00/0x02-0x06. (2) dji_sys's direct, literal-immediate duss_event_register_dynamic_command call sites (11 total, confirmed by `blx 9bd0 <duss_event_register_dynamic_command@plt>` xrefs): 3x cmd_set 0x22/cmd_id 0x60 (Demo Mode, matches prior doc04 finding), 2x cmd_set 0x00/cmd_id 0xa3 (USB State Report, matches catalog), 2x cmd_set 0x06/cmd_id 0x3a, 1x cmd_set 0x04/cmd_id 0x69 -- none under cmd_set 0x00 match 0x02-0x06. (3) The remaining 2 of those 11 call sites (vaddr 0x2da62 and 0x70048 in dji_sys) are NOT literal-immediate: they loop over a runtime-populated table of {cmd_set, N cmd_ids, shared handler} sub-tables, reading cmd_set from a per-table field and cmd_id from array position -- architecturally exactly the shape the task describes for a generic cross-chip param bus. Traced the table pointer back to a lazily-initialized .bss global, which in turn traces to three custom ELF sections literally named `param_manager_local` (0xa8250, 56 bytes), `param_manager_buf_local` (0xa8288, 32 bytes) and `param_manager_remote` (0xa82a8, 12 bytes) in dji_sys -- strong confirmation a real 'Param Manager' subsystem exists and matches ~40 'PM:'-prefixed debug strings describing a hash-keyed named-parameter protocol with push-frequency subscriptions and remote get/set (e.g. 'PM:register remote param item err, name: %s, freq: %d', 'PM:recieved push remote param hash was not register, hash: %u', 'PM:request_remote_param_fix_send failed, freq: %d, ret: %d'). However: (a) param_manager_local on this specific image contains only one populated entry (name 'sysmode_param_block'), (b) I could not resolve which literal (cmd_set, cmd_id) values the data-driven loop registers for it (the loop itself derives them from table position/fields at runtime, not a literal I could read statically with confidence), and (c) repeated attempts to find the actual wire-payload-parsing function by cross-referencing the 'PM:' debug strings (both the standard PIC ldr+add-pc idiom and a direct absolute-pointer scan) found zero code xrefs within this pass's effort -- these strings appear to be reached through a call path this method could not resolve (possibly a shared format-string table indexed by id rather than per-callsite literal pool loads). I did not invent a field layout without this evidence. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Set SDK Std Msgs Frequency
note: Checked all 4 known registration mechanisms with no match. (a) Literal-immediate scan: wrote a capstone-based scanner that resolves the PLT stub for duss_event_register_dynamic_command[_with_user_data] in an ELF, finds every bl/blx call site to it (Thumb mode with skipdata=True to survive embedded literal pools), and reads back the preceding literal r1(cmd_set)/r2(cmd_id) immediates. Ran it against dji_sys (E1E 32-bit: 11 real call sites recovered, matching and reproducing this project's already-known mappings for 0x22/0x60, 0x00/0xa3, 0x06/0x3a, 0x04/0x69 exactly -- validating the method) and again, independently, in AArch64 against dji_sys (E2: 12 call sites, same four known mappings reproduced). Then ran the same scanner over every 32-bit ELF in e1e_extracted/system_files/{bin,lib,xbin} (all daemons and shared libs, not just dji_sys). No call site anywhere registers cmd_set 0 / cmd_id 0x10. (b) libduml_frwk.so's one built-in 6-entry dynamic-command data table (vaddr 0x1098fc in E1E, independently re-decoded by hand from readelf -x .data this round) does not contain 0x10 either (its 6 entries are cmd_id 0x00, 0x2f, 0x89, 0xfa, 0xaa, and cmd_set 0x51/0x05). (c) dji_flight, dji_navigation and dji_autoflight (the plausible owners of an SDK telemetry-frequency command) import only duss_mb_create_route_table/duss_event_create_client -- they do not import duss_event_register_dynamic_command at all, so if 0x10 lives there it is wired through the string/route-tag-keyed mechanism in note (d), not a literal cmd_id. (d) In dji_sys (E1E) I found a previously-undocumented local helper at vaddr 0x6fff4 that loops over an externally-supplied table of {cmd_set:u16, cmd_id:u16, pad:u32} rows (stride 12 bytes) and calls duss_event_register_dynamic_command once per row, all sharing one fixed handler descriptor -- this is a batch-registration mechanism this project had not previously documented, and it is architecturally capable of covering 0x10. However I could not find any caller of this helper (a full skipdata-enabled scan of dji_sys's .text for bl/blx targeting 0x6fff4/0x6fff5 found zero hits, and a raw byte search for its address as a relocated function-pointer-table entry also found zero hits), so its actual table contents -- and therefore whether 0x10 is one of its rows -- could not be recovered. This is a concrete lead for a future pass, not a resolved finding. Given all of the above, I did not invent a payload layout. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: File List
note: Per the task hint, checked whether 0x20-0x28 share the already-partially-known cmd_set 0x00/0x2A 'FileTrans General Trans' transport. Confirmed by direct disassembly (both E1E armv7 and E2 aarch64 libduml_frwk.so -- addresses match 1:1 across builds) that duss_file_trans_event (E1E vaddr 0x8f515) is a tiny dispatcher that reads ONE byte from the incoming message at the same struct offset (+0x14) that this project's existing Lua dissector already uses as payload offset 0 ('Transfer Phase') for cmd 0x2A, and branches: phase 1 -> bl duss_file_trans_req (0x8d970, the already-documented 'start transfer' path), phase 2 -> bl duss_file_trans_data (0x8e155, matches the already-documented partno+data path), phase 3 -> bl duss_file_trans_checksum (0x8ef79, matches the already-documented 16-byte 'after transfer' path), phase 4 -> bl duss_file_trans_data_lost_list (0x8e661, a 4th phase NOT in the existing 0x2A dissector at all -- a new finding, semantically a good match for 'File Segment Err'/0x25, but see below). This re-confirms and extends the shared-module architecture, but does NOT by itself tell us which literal cmd_id(s) besides 0x2A route into it. I then checked all 6 daemons previously identified as consumers of this module (dji_sys, dji_perception, dji_blackbox, dji_config_store, dji_sec, libupgrade_commu_demo.so): every one of them imports duss_file_trans_event only via an R_ARM_ABS32 relocation landing in a .data struct field (confirmed exact relocated offsets in dji_sys: 0xa5e24, and in dji_blackbox: 0x3de70) that is consumed by duss_mb_create_route_table/duss_event_create_client -- the route-tag/string-keyed mechanism, not a literal register_dynamic_command(cmd_set,cmd_id,...) call. I disassembled dji_blackbox's duss_event_create_client call site (vaddr 0x5ffa) and duss_mb_create_route_table call site (0x5e64) directly: the fields populated into the route-table/client-config structs there are pointer-sized (string/pointer) values and small integers that are NOT DUML cmd_id bytes (e.g. literal ints 7 and 0x32 at specific struct offsets, plus several relocated pointers I could not confirm as readable C-strings in the time available). Ran the same full literal-immediate scanner from 0x10's entry across every 32-bit daemon/lib in the firmware (bin+lib+xbin) specifically for cmd_set 0/cmd_id in {0x20,0x21,0x22,0x23,0x25,0x26,0x28}: zero hits anywhere. This reconfirms, independently, this project's own prior conclusion in 14_FOLLOWUP_DEEPDIVE_FINDINGS.md Track E ('Not determined: the exact cmd_id(s) bound to duss_file_trans_event per consuming daemon') -- I was not able to go further than that prior pass on the specific cmd_id binding, despite a fresh, independent attempt. I did not invent a payload layout for 0x20 specifically; its name ('File List') is also the one in this batch I'd trust LEAST to actually be this same chunked-transfer state machine (a directory listing is a plausible, semantically distinct, simpler request/response that could have an entirely different handler I did not find). See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Safe Communication
note: Name-matched a local function `sys_event_security_comm` at vaddr 0x41310 (8 bytes: `mov w0,#-0x3f3; ret` — an unconditional-error stub that never reads its arguments at all). Its address is taken via an R_AARCH64_RELATIVE relocation at .data offset 0xf1050, sitting in the same irregularly-strided region of relocated function pointers that also holds sys_event_set_date/sys_event_rtc_get_date/sys_event_power_manage_req (i.e. it IS part of dji_sys's General-command handler-context blob, not random data) — but I could not find the code that actually WALKS this region by cmd_id: a full linear disassembly of dji_sys's .text (both E2/AArch64 and E1E/ARM32-Thumb, using capstone with skipdata to survive embedded literal pools) found only 11-12 literal-immediate `duss_event_register_dynamic_command(client,cmd_set,cmd_id,ctx)` call sites total in each binary, all of which match ALREADY-documented commands (0x00/0xa3, 0x22/0x60, 0x06/0x3a, 0x04/0x69) — none of them is 0x34. I also chased what I first thought was an adjacent sub-dispatcher at 0x41318 (reads a payload byte, checks range 0x40-0x44) hoping it was 0x34- or fw-update-related, but its 'in-range' branch target (vaddr 0x837e0) resolves to the unrelated, clearly-named `clear_log_all_process` — so that code is almost certainly part of a Log-Control command (0xF2/0xF3/0xFA), not Safe Communication or the fw-update range, and I'm flagging that red herring explicitly so a future pass doesn't re-walk it. Net result: a plausible but unproven handler candidate, which — even if correctly attributed — contains no payload fields to decode (it unconditionally rejects before touching the message). See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Fw Update Desc Push
note: Per this project's own `20_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_PROCESS_FINDINGS.md` (Track BF) and `cmdset_00_General.md`'s binary-investigation note, 0x40 and 0x43 were the two of the original 7-command fw-update gap that remained fully unresolved even after that dedicated sweep (0x07/0x08/0x09/0x0A/0x41 were at least confirmed sender-side). Per this round's explicit instruction to look harder at dji_sys's FULL register table directly rather than trust the prior search radius: I did a complete linear disassembly of dji_sys's entire .text section on BOTH architectures (E2/AArch64 via capstone CS_ARCH_ARM64; E1E/ARM32 via capstone CS_ARCH_ARM+CS_MODE_THUMB with skipdata=True to survive literal-pool desync — the default thumb decode silently stopped after ~240 bytes without that flag, which I caught and fixed), located the real PLT stub address for `duss_event_register_dynamic_command` on each architecture (computed from the ARM32 PLT's two-ADD GOT-relative addressing by hand since no disassembler resolves it directly), and enumerated EVERY `bl`/`blx` call site to that stub in the whole binary. Result: 12 call sites in E2, 11 in E1E, and in both cases every single one resolves (via the literal `mov w1,#cmd_set; mov w2,#cmd_id` immediates I decoded alongside it) to an ALREADY-documented command (0x00/0xa3, 0x22/0x60, 0x06/0x3a, 0x04/0x69) — none is 0x40. This rules out the direct/literal-immediate registration mechanism for 0x40 in dji_sys on both chips, which is strictly more thorough than the prior pass's stated search. It does not rule out a loop/table-driven registration (dji_sys has at least two such loops, e.g. `sys_command_agent_config`, that pull cmd_set/cmd_id from a runtime array rather than a literal immediate, which my scan cannot resolve without walking that array's actual runtime contents) — that remains a genuine, acknowledged gap, not a disproof. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Get Temperature Info
note: Found via the dispatch table (row 0x54 = 0xf0b70+0x54*0x18=0xf1350 -> fn=0x41e60). Confirmed by .gnu_debugdata symbol name sys_event_get_temp_info @ 0x41e60 and 5 embedded log/format strings: 'sys_event_get_temp_info' (0xa7aba), 'get_temp_info msg_len %d error' (0xa8938), 'get_temp_info not support this platform' (0xa8957), 'get_omc_handle failed' (0xa897f), and 'get_temp_info input msg error, %d should <= %d' (0xa8995). Disassembled the full body (vaddr 0x41e60-0x4209c): it first checks the incoming message's length field (struct offset 0x10) equals exactly 1, erroring otherwise ('get_temp_info msg_len %d error', resp code 0xff). It then requires the platform's power-module identity string (compared via strncmp against a constant read as 'PM430S AC') to match, erroring 'get_temp_info not support this platform' otherwise -- i.e. this handler only functions on hardware carrying that specific power module. It then calls sys_omc_get_this_board_handle() and sys_omc_get_temp() (both confirmed by symbol name) to obtain/refresh a per-channel sensor-data structure. It then reads the single payload byte at struct offset 0x14 (same payload-start convention validated for 0x51/0x5B) as a channel index, rejecting values >= 6 ('get_temp_info input msg error, %d should <= %d', resp code 0xff). For index 5 it reads one raw byte directly from the board-handle struct at offset 0x55; for indices 0-4 it reads a 32-bit float from the struct at offset (index*4)+0x40 and truncates it to a signed integer. Either way the resulting integer is multiplied by 10 (via add+shift: x+x*4, then <<1) and returned as a 16-bit value through duss_event_resp_data(), response length fixed at 2 bytes. Which physical sensor each index 0-4 corresponds to (battery/ESC/board/etc.) could not be determined from this function alone -- the surrounding 'temperature_group'/'omc' subsystem in this binary tracks many named channels (esc_temperature_group, bat_temperature_group, cb_temperature_group, and about a dozen more, per embedded JSON-config-key strings), but this specific 6-slot board-handle array was not traced to that naming scheme with confidence, so the index is reported generically rather than guessed. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

note: No handler for cmd_set 0x00/cmd_id 0x58 could be located by any of this project's four known registration mechanisms. Concretely: (1) exhaustively enumerated every literal-immediate duss_event_register_dynamic_command call site in dji_sys on BOTH architectures (11 call sites in e1e/ARM32 Thumb at vaddr range 0x2db80-0x70064, 12 in e2/aarch64 at 0x2db80-0x96f8c, cross-checked register-argument values programmatically) -- none registers cmd_set=0 with cmd_id=0x58; the only cmd_set=0 literal registration found anywhere is cmd_id 0xa3 (already-known USB State Report). (2) dji_sys (e2/aarch64) also contains a 256-slot array, directly indexed by single-byte cmd_id, of {primary_handler_fn, secondary/ack_fn, flag} 24-byte records for cmd_set 0x00 (confirmed real by independently re-deriving 3 already-documented cmd_ids from it: 0x54='Get Temperature Info' -> sys_event_get_temp_info, exact name match to this project's existing doc; 0x5B='FTP Control' -> sys_event_ftpd_control, matches this project's doc20 finding; 0x60='Auto Test Info' -> sys_event_auto_test_info, see that entry below). This strongly suggests the dissector's 'Time Sync' label on cmd_id 0x58 does not correspond to dji_sys's real on-wire time-sync traffic, which runs on 0x68 instead; 0x58 may belong to a different/legacy mechanism or an as-yet-unexamined daemon. However, this string table reads as flight-record/blackbox field-definition metadata (an 'Op.expr' naming/expression scheme, most likely used by dji_flight's or a ground-station tool's log decoder to extract named values from a raw telemetry/black-box stream) rather than code that reads or writes DUML wire bytes for cmd_id 0x45 specifically -- I found no function that reads these 17 values from an incoming request buffer or writes them into a response buffer with a cmd-0x45-keyed call site. Given neither piece of evidence confirms the actual wire-level shape (fixed-length 17/64-element array vs. a visible-satellite-count-prefixed variable list, whether each entry is exactly 1 byte, or whether there are accompanying per-channel ID/elevation/azimuth fields as real GNSS SNR reports commonly carry), I'm reporting this as insufficient_evidence rather than asserting an offset table, per the project's rule against inventing layouts -- but recording the strong architectural signal for whoever revisits this command. No duss_event_register_dynamic_command call site (literal or packed-cmd-word) for cmd_set 0x03/cmd_id 0xba was found in dji_flight, dji_sys (E1E ARM32 or E2 AArch64), dji_navigation, or dji_autoflight. dji_flight's relocated {func_ptr,cmd_word} dispatch array at vaddr 0xae038 (fully decoded, see shared_infrastructure_found) has no 0x03/0xba row. dji_flight imports zero duss_event_register_dynamic_command-family symbols at all (confirmed via readelf -rW and --dyn-syms: no PLT/JUMP_SLOT, no dynsym entry), so this cmd cannot be registered there directly.

Concrete lead found, not confirmed: dji_sys (E2/AArch64 build only) has a real function `led_control_thread` (vaddr 0x44960, recovered by name from .gnu_debugdata minidebuginfo; decompiled/decompressed and cross-checked against the live binary's own bytes). Its single argument is read as a 4-byte struct: byte0 bit1 = a gate/enable flag (tbz w8,#1 branches to the no-op exit if clear); byte1 = a 3-valued mode enum (0,1,2 - any other nonzero value also falls to the no-op exit); byte2 and byte3 = per-zone boolean flags, each independently logged if nonzero (consistent with 'forearm'=multiple LED positions/arms). Mode 2's branch additionally builds the 32-bit constant 0x7a120 (500000) passed to a call at vaddr 0x10110 (plausibly a delay/sleep primitive), consistent with a timed blink pattern. This 4-byte shape (enable_flag_bit, mode_enum, zone2_flag, zone3_flag) is a very plausible candidate for this command's payload, but: (1) no caller of led_control_thread (static bl/blx xref, or any relocation pointing at 0x44960) was found anywhere in the binary -- it is presumably invoked only via a runtime function-pointer table populated from dji_sys's own local JSON startup-config file (the same non-statically-enumerable mechanism this project already documented in 04_WM260_DAEMON_FINDINGS.md for cmd_set 0x10), so the exact byte-for-byte binding to cmd_id 0xba (vs. some other LED-adjacent cmd_id, or no DUML binding at all) is NOT confirmed; (2) the function does not exist at all in the E1E/ARM32 dji_sys build (checked directly), so this lead is architecture-specific. Reported as a lead, not a decode. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Open Led Action Logout
note:
Handler SUBSYSTEM is confirmed with high confidence; the exact REQUEST wire-payload layout is not. `sys_fc_logout_led_ctrl_action` (dji_sys, E2/AArch64, vaddr 0x37548, size 828, name from .gnu_debugdata symtab) directly constructs the literal 32-bit value 0x000300bd (bytes: cmd_id=0xbd, cmd_set=0x03 packed as cmd_set<<16|cmd_id, via `mov w8,#0xbd` + `movk w8,#0x3,lsl #16` at vaddr 0x37600/0x37608) as part of an OUTGOING confirmation message it builds on the stack and sends via a call to the generic send primitive at PLT slot 0xf5c0 (`duss_event_send_sync`). This is the ONLY place in the whole dji_sys(E2) binary (and the only one of the project's whole-binary mov+movk-0x3<<16 sweep's 7 hits, 6 of which are genuine cmd_set-0x03 constructions -- see shared_infrastructure_found) where cmd_id 0xbd appears bound to cmd_set 0x03 this concretely -- this is a strong, real, disassembly-confirmed binding, not a name guess.

However, `sys_fc_logout_led_ctrl_action`'s single input argument (x19) is NOT read as raw wire bytes in this function -- it is read at offset+4 (loaded, then stored into the outgoing message as a uint16) and offset+8/+9 (two individual bytes, read once early on purely for a debug-log argument) -- i.e. x19 looks like a small, already-parsed per-client 'LED action registration record' (populated earlier by the Register path, 0xbc), not a fresh copy of this request's own wire payload. The function's only confirmed caller is `sys_fc_led_exit` (vaddr 0x37888, an internal cleanup/teardown routine, itself with no found caller either) -- so whether x19 is populated directly from this specific 0xbd request's payload, or is looked up by some other key (a connection/client id) with 0xbd carrying little or no payload of its own, could not be determined from static analysis alone. Reporting the struct offsets found (+4: 2 bytes used as uint16; +8: 1 byte; +9: 1 byte, log-only) as a lead, not asserting them as the confirmed wire layout. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

fields.desc: Fourth value in the same debug string ('type = %d'). Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x18 (24). Semantic enumeration not recovered.

fields.name: host_id_count
fields.label: Host ID Count (operation=2 only)
fields.desc: Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x19 (25). Used directly both as the loop bound for, and to decide whether to execute, the host_id_list array below (confirmed on both architecture builds: a cmp/bls-style bound check against this exact byte gates the per-entry 'RS: route switch host id = %#x' log loop).

fields.name: host_id_list
fields.label: Host ID List (operation=2 only)
fields.type: uint16[] (little-endian, 2 bytes per element, repeated host_id_count times)
fields.desc: Array of little-endian 16-bit host IDs starting at struct offset +0x1a (26), each individually logged via 'RS: route switch host id = %#x'. 2-byte element stride independently confirmed on both builds: AArch64 indexes as `ldrh w4,[x28, x27, lsl #1]` with x28 = base+0x1a; ARM32 indexes identically as `ldrh.w r2,[ip, #26]` with ip = base + (index*2). Total field size is 2*host_id_count bytes; the size shown here (2) is for a single element.
